elements.name: Chat reply flow to authenticated requester

controls.name: Read only least privilege credential to policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Credential scope does not decay with model capability; the agent cannot write to or read beyond the policy index.

controls.name: Verified network layer egress deny
controls.decay_rationale: Network egress deny is enforced outside the model and remains effective regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Replies bound to authenticated requester session only
controls.decay_rationale: The reply destination is fixed by the authenticated chat session rather than model output, so the model cannot redirect responses to another recipient.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Client behavior removes common hidden egress channels regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Two person review before policy publication
controls.decay_rationale: The publication workflow is outside the model and reduces unauthorized tampering of policy content.

controls.name: Pinned model with change ticket required for model change
controls.decay_rationale: Model changes require formal review and do not occur silently.

controls.name: Attributable audit record for agent replies
controls.decay_rationale: Recommended tamper evident action records would restore reply provenance without relying on model compliance.

findings.title: Missing attributable action record for autonomous replies

forecast.watch_signal: No change in tier from the considered triggers; reassess if reply logging or attribution design is introduced or if reply scope changes.

evidence.observation: The design states the agent answers without approval and describes no audit record, provenance store, or tamper evident log that attributes replies to the agent.

recommendations.action: Add tamper evident, attributable action records for each autonomous reply, including requester identity, retrieved policy source, quoted passages, and agent action metadata.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not describe the chat service authentication path to the agent process itself, only that employee chat is SSO authenticated.
The design exposes no spend, execute, delegation, memory, or open ended runtime path; it is a single reply policy QA agent with one read only tool.
The artifacts say employee chat is SSO authenticated but do not provide protocol or session binding details to assess spoofing resistance fully.
The design does not describe requester side logging or nonrepudiation records for employee submissions.
The publication workflow names two person review but does not describe identity verification controls for HR content team authors.
The artifacts do not describe publication audit records for HR content team actions in the policy workflow.
The artifacts do not describe availability protections, quotas, or recovery characteristics for the policy index.
This input flow is described as an internal authenticated chat path and does not cross a trust boundary in the assessed design representation.
This input flow is represented as staying within the first party trust domain and is not a boundary crossing flow in this assessment.
The flow is a bounded employee chat request path with no exposed external protocol boundary described in the artifacts.
This retrieval flow is represented as internal to the first party environment and not a trust boundary crossing data flow.
The policy retrieval path stays within the same trust domain and is not described as crossing an external boundary.
The artifacts provide no cross boundary protocol edge here; availability of this internal flow is outside the assessed design detail.
The reply flow is bound to the authenticated requester session and is represented as remaining within the first party chat environment.
The reply flow does not cross a trust boundary in this design because it is confined to the authenticated requester's in product chat session.
This is a bounded internal chat response path with no boundary crossing protocol edge described for STRIDE flow analysis.

rating.rationale: No present untrusted source reaches a sensitive sink, and strong structural controls sever external egress and recipient redirection for replies. The remaining notable issue is a moderate property finding: the design does not describe attributable audit records for autonomous replies. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration artifacts provided, not observed runtime behavior.

No source code, IaC, or live runtime configuration was provided, so authentication path details, logging implementation, and exact network enforcement were assessed from runtime notes rather than direct verification except where the notes state pen test verification.
Because the design describes no memory, no protocol peers, and no additional tools, the assessment confidence is limited to the provided scope and would change if those capabilities are later added.
